text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 6.2% today following a sharp reversal in oil prices driven by diplomatic developments in the Middle East conflict. After oil prices spiked to a six-month high of $116+ just days ago on escalating Iran-Israel tensions, news on October 26–27 of peace discussions between Iran's leadership and Saudi officials triggered a selloff—crude dropped below $108, and refiners like Marathon felt the pressure as the margin between crude input costs and fuel output prices compressed.

The bigger picture here is that refiners profit most when crude prices stay elevated but stable; wild swings from geopolitical risk create uncertainty. Over two weeks, Marathon has lost 7.4% as investors cycled out of the "war premium" baked into oil prices during the height of tensions, even though U.S. refinery utilization remains healthy at 93.4%.
